corpus.title: O furacão que colocou litoral do México em alerta em meio ao 'super El Niño'
corpus.signal_text:
O furacão que colocou litoral do México em alerta em meio ao 'super El Niño'
  - Author, Redação
  - Role, BBC News Mundo
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 4 min
O furacão Polo, que tinha atingido a categoria 5 na terça-feira (22/09), tornando-se uma das tempestades que mais rapidamente se intensificaram na história do oceano Pacífico — desde que se tem registro disso — colocou o litoral do México em estado de alerta.
Segundo o Centro Nacional de Furacões dos EUA (NHC, na sigla em inglês), o Polo atingiu ventos de 270 km/h na noite de terça-feira, o que o colocou na categoria de furacão de categoria 5, o nível máximo na Escala Saffir-Simpson. No decorrer da madrugada, entretanto, ele perdeu força e foi rebaixado para categoria 4; com ventos de até 250 km/h, ele continua sendo perigoso e destrutivo.
Nas próximas horas, está previsto que ele se desloque para o noroeste, paralelamente à costa mexicana do Pacífico.
Essa trajetória evitará, por enquanto, um impacto direto sobre as populações costeiras, mas provocará fortes chuvas e riscos de inundações e deslizamentos de terra.
Segundo o Serviço Meteorológico Nacional do México (SMN), são previstas rajadas de vento de 70 a 90 km/h e ondas de 7,0 a 9,0 metros de altura nas costas de Colima, Michoacán e Guerrero; bem como ondas de 2,0 a 3,0 metros de altura nas costas de Jalisco e Oaxaca.
Segundo o NHC, embora a evolução de sua trajetória o leve a se deslocar próximo à costa mexicana nos próximos dias, seu comportamento poderá mudar.
"Ainda existe incerteza sobre quão próximo o furacão chegará da costa, e parece provável que haja alguns impactos de vento, chuva e ressaca", afirmou o NHC.
As autoridades educacionais anunciaram a suspensão das aulas em municípios do litoral de Guerrero e Michoacán nesta terça e quarta-feira.
"Por favor, toda a população da costa do Pacífico deve permanecer muito atenta. Até agora, são chuvas intensas... Não parece que vá atingir a terra diretamente", disse a presidente do México, Claudia Sheinbaum, em sua coletiva matinal.
Intensificação rápida
Alguns meteorologistas destacaram que o Polo se intensificou desde sua classificação como tempestade tropical até a categoria 5 em cerca de 36 horas.
Isso o coloca entre os três fenômenos que mais rapidamente se fortaleceram até a categoria máxima da escala Saffir-Simpson, ao lado dos furacões Otis (2023) e Patricia (2015).
E, como ocorreu na década passada no caso do Patricia, o furacão Polo chega impulsionado pela presença do fenômeno El Niñ

corpus.title: Hurricane Polo in the Pacific Ocean considered 'one of the strongest storms ever'
corpus.signal_text:
Hurricane Polo in the Pacific Ocean considered 'one of the strongest storms ever'
Polo not expected to make landfall, but its gathering strength is 'truly remarkable,' storm researcher says
Hurricane Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades and was expected to skirt Mexico's southwestern coast as a Category 5 storm.
Polo was an "extremely dangerous" storm, with maximum sustained winds of 265 km/h, the U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami said Tuesday night.
Polo was nearly stationary early Wednesday, about 300 kilometres south of Zihuatanejo in Guerrero state and 540 kilometres southeast of Manzanillo, moving north at four kilometres per hour with maximum sustained winds of 255 km/h, the centre reported.
It was forecast to turn sharply to the northwest during the day and then move in west-northwest over the next several days.
U.S. National Hurricane Center data shows Polo's winds reached speeds comparable to only a few hurricanes in the region in recent decades, primarily Hurricane Patricia, which had winds that reached 346 km/h in 2015.
"This is one of the strongest storms ever in the [Pacific] Basin," said Kristen L. Corbosiero, professor at the University at Albany's department of atmospheric and environmental sciences.
The rapid intensification of the storm has stunned scientists and authorities alike, with the NHC writing in a report that it was "truly remarkable" how quickly Polo gained strength in the past 24 hours.
Phil Klotzbach, research scientist in the department of atmospheric science at Colorado State University, attributed the intensification to the weather phenomenon known as El Niño, which has fuelled crippling droughts in Mexico and Central America and floods in other parts of the region.
In the Pacific, it has resulted in warmer waters and wind patterns that act as fodder for hurricanes, he said.
"There are all the ingredients that hurricanes need to get really strong really fast," Klotzbach said.
Warnings of life-threatening flooding
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said experts indicated that the hurricane was not likely to touch land. Still, hurricane-force winds extend up to 65 kilometres from the storm's centre and tropical storm-force winds up to 169 kilometres from the eye, the U.S. centre said.

corpus.title: Polo off Mexican coast grows into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades
corpus.signal_text:
Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades and was expected to skirt Mexico’s southwestern coast as a major hurricane, while another Pacific system, Odalys, strengthened Wednesday from a tropical storm to a hurricane without threatening land.
The U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami has called Polo an “extremely dangerous” storm and forecast the system would turn sharply to the northwest before moving west-northwest over the next several days.
Polo was about 266 kilometres south of Zihuatanejo and 515 kilometres southeast of Manzanillo moving north at four kph with maximum sustained winds of 241 kph, the center reported. That put it near the top of Category 4 strength, after earlier being a Category 5 storm.
“Fluctuations in intensity are expected, but Polo is expected to remain a very powerful major hurricane during the next few days,” the NHC said.
Odalys was a Category 1 hurricane and was about 2,085 kilometres off the southern tip of the Baja California peninsula of Mexico, moving east-northeast at 15 kph with maximum sustained winds of 120 kph, the hurricane center said.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said experts indicated Polo was not likely to touch land. Still, hurricane-force winds extend up to 65 kilometres from the storm’s center and tropical storm-force winds up to 169 kilometres from the eye, the U.S. center said.
Tropical storm conditions were expected along the Pacific coast in Guerrero, Michoacan and Colima states Wednesday into Thursday.
The hurricane set residents along Mexico's Pacific coast on edge once again after being walloped by powerful cyclones a number of times in recent years. Beaches emptied out and dark clouds swirled above choppy seas, while Mexican authorities temporarily suspended classes Tuesday in a number of areas.
The Associated Press
Polo on Tuesday became the third Category 5 hurricane of the Pacific season, following Genevieve and Lowell earlier this year. Category 5 is the highest level on the Saffir-Simpson scale, reflecting that a storm has maximum sustained winds exceeding 253 kph.
